newsitem.title: BURMA: Petrol prices soar in Burma on talk of shortage.
newsitem.headline: Petrol prices soar in Burma on talk of shortage.

text.p: Petrol and diesel prices soared on the Burmese black market on panic buying as consumers feared shortages, a government official and consumers said on Thursday.

A gallon of petrol on the black market was selling for 400-420 kyats on Thursday, compared with 180-200 kyats about a month ago. On the black market, one dollar bought about 170 kyats on Thursday while the official rate is about six kyat to the dollar.

"It is panic buying, because of rumours," a ministry of energy official told Reuters. "Rumours are circulating that a company supplying crude to Myanmar (Burma) stopped...and car owners are worried about supply."
"But things will calm down soon," he said. "We reduced supply to private buses and school ferry cars who used to make much profit by selling their surplus to the black market."
As a result, the flow of illegal petrol onto the black market was cut, he said.
Rumours have been circulating in Rangoon that a foreign company recently stopped supplying crude to Burma.
Some consumers also noted there had been a huge rise in the number of imported reconditioned Japanese cars in Rangoon over the past year, causing a sharp increase in fuel demand.
On Saturday democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi told supporters the military government owed $31 million to a foreign company supplying essential chemicals, which is why supplies stopped.
Japan's Mitsui, a key supplier of crude to Burma, on Thursday said it had fulfilled all obligations of its contract, which expired earlier this month.
A spokesman told Reuters in Tokyo he could not immediately say if Burma had completed its payments to Mitsui.
Petrol consumers and filling station employees in Rangoon said prices had been rising over the past few weeks as rumours of possible shortages began to spread.
Private car owners often have to rely on the black market to top up their tanks as most are only permitted to buy two gallons of petrol a week at the official price of 25 kyats per gallon.
Previously a consumer could buy as much petrol as he wanted on the black market if he was willing to pay the price.
But last week petrol stations in Rangoon set a limit of four gallons per person per week. Many petrol stations quickly sold out of their daily petrol supplies early in the day, employees said.
